extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies, pass-through entities, recipients and subrecipients of Federal awards, auditors, and grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Authoritative list of terms and their definitions used throughout 2 CFR part 200 (OMB Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards). Used to interpret requirements for Federal financial assistance, awards, audits, and related administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the (total) cost of the asset including the cost to ready the asset for its intended use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for equipment, the net invoice price including modifications, attachments, accessories, or auxiliary apparatus necessary to make it usable; software includes development costs capitalized under GAAP. Ancillary charges such as taxes, duty, insurance, freight, and installation may be included or excluded per recipient's regular accounting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a payment that a Federal agency or pass-through entity makes by any appropriate payment mechanism and payment method before the recipient or subrecipient disburses the funds for program purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the process of assigning a cost, or a group of costs, to one or more cost objective(s) in reasonable proportion to the benefit provided or other equitable relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May assign costs directly to a final cost objective or through intermediate cost objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance Listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to the publicly available listing of Federal assistance programs managed and administered by the GSA at SAM.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance Listing number
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a unique number assigned to identify an Assistance Listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance Listing program title
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the title that corresponds to the Assistance Listing number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit finding
rubrics_metrics.description: Means deficiencies which the auditor is required to report in the schedule of findings and questioned costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §200.516(a) for reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditee
rubrics_metrics.description: Means any non-Federal entity that must be audited under this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §200.501 for audit thresholds and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditor
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an auditor who is a public accountant or a Federal, State, local government, or Indian Tribe audit organization that meets GAGAS standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include internal auditors of nonprofit organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the financial plan for the Federal award that the Federal agency or pass-through entity approves during the Federal award process or in subsequent amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include Federal and non-Federal share or only the Federal share as determined by the agency or pass-through entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget period
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the time interval from the start date of a funded portion of an award to the end date of that funded portion during which recipients/subrecipients are authorized to incur obligations of the funds awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes any funds carried forward or other revisions under §200.308.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Tangible or intangible assets used in operations having a useful life of more than one year which are capitalized in accordance with GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes land, buildings, equipment, intellectual property (including software), and additions/improvements that materially increase value or useful life. Excludes intangible right-to-use assets and right-to-use operating lease assets per GASB/FASB (see §200.465).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenditures to acquire capital assets or to make additions, improvements, modifications, replacements, rearrangements, reinstallations, renovations, or alterations to capital assets that materially increase their value or useful life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central service cost allocation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation identifying, accumulating, and allocating or developing billing rates based on allowable costs of services provided centrally by a State, local government, or Indian Tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs may be allocated or billed to users; used to distribute central service costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on context, either (1) a written demand or assertion seeking payment, adjustment/interpretation of terms, or other relief under a Federal award, or (2) a request for payment not in dispute when submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class of Federal awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a group of Federal awards awarded under a program or to a type of recipient to which specific provisions or exceptions may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the process by which the Federal agency or pass-through entity determines that all applicable administrative actions and all required work of the Federal award have been completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions described in §200.344 guide the closeout process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cluster of programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a grouping of closely related programs that share common compliance requirements (types: R&D, SFA, and other clusters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clusters are treated as one program when determining major programs (§200.518); States designating 'other clusters' must identify included awards and advise subrecipients consistent with §200.332.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognizant agency for audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the Federal agency designated to carry out responsibilities described in §200.513(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not necessarily the same as cognizant agency for indirect costs. Single Audit contacts listed at the Federal Audit Clearinghouse website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognizant agency for indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the Federal agency responsible for reviewing, negotiating and approving cost allocation plans or indirect cost proposals on behalf of all Federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments vary by recipient type: IHEs (Appendix III C.11), nonprofits (Appendix IV C.2.a), State/local governments (Appendix V F.1), Indian Tribes (Appendix VII D.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: An annually updated authoritative source for auditors identifying important compliance requirements expected to be considered as part of an audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors use it to understand program objectives, procedures, compliance requirements, audit objectives, and suggested audit procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Means machines that acquire, store, analyze, process, and publish data electronically, including accessories for printing, transmitting/receiving, or storing electronic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also definitions of supplies and information technology systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of Federal financial assistance, a legal instrument by which a recipient or subrecipient conducts procurement transactions under a Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §200.331 for subrecipient vs contractor determinations; see definition of subaward in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an entity that receives a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the second or subsequent budget period within an identified period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperative agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal instrument of financial assistance used to transfer anything of value to carry out a public purpose and distinguished from a grant by substantial involvement of the Federal agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include cooperative R&D agreements under 15 U.S.C. 3710a or agreements that provide only direct cash assistance to individuals, subsidies, loans, loan guarantees, or insurance. Consistent with 31 U.S.C. 6302-6305 and 31 U.S.C. 6101(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: Action taken by the auditee that corrects identified deficiencies, produces recommended improvements, or demonstrates that audit findings are invalid or do not warrant action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost allocation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a central service or public assistance cost allocation plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a program, function, activity, award, organizational subdivision, contract, or work unit for which cost data are desired and accumulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be a major function, service, project, Federal award, or indirect cost activity (see subpart E). See also final and intermediate cost objective definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the portion of project costs not paid by Federal funds or contributions (unless authorized by statute). Includes matching which refers to required levels of cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §200.306 for cost sharing/matching requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Means charges to a Federal award that the Federal agency or pass-through entity determines to be unallowable in accordance with statutes, regulations, this part, or terms/conditions of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary award
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an award where the Federal agency exercises judgment in selecting the recipient or amount of funding through competitive processes or merit, consistent with statutory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be selected on a non-competitive basis where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tangible personal property (including information technology systems) with useful life >1 year and per-unit acquisition cost at or above the lesser of recipient's capitalization level or $10,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See capital assets, computing devices, general purpose equipment, information technology systems, special purpose equipment, and supplies for distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges made by a recipient or subrecipient to a project for which a Federal award is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be reported on cash or accrual basis if methodology disclosed and consistently applied. Cash-basis and accrual-basis components for computation are specified in the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an 'agency' as defined at 5 U.S.C. 551(1) and clarified by 5 U.S.C. 552(f); generally refers to the agency providing a Federal award directly to a recipient unless context indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See definitions of Federal award and recipient for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Audit Clearinghouse (FAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository of record designated by OMB where non-Federal entities must transmit information required by subpart F (Single Audit reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal award
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on context, either (1) Federal financial assistance or cost-reimbursement contract received directly or indirectly, or (2) the instrument setting forth terms and conditions (grant agreement, cooperative agreement, other assistance agreement, or cost-reimbursement contract).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include other contracts used to buy goods/services or GOCO facility operation contracts. See definitions of federal financial assistance, grant agreement, and cooperative agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal award date
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the date when the authorized official of the Federal agency signed the Federal award (physically or digitally) or when an alternative consistent with 31 U.S.C. 1501 is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance recipients or subrecipients receive or administer in forms such as grants, cooperative agreements, non-cash contributions/donations, direct appropriations, food commodities, and other financial assistance (with certain exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain sections expand the definition to include loans, loan guarantees, interest subsidies, insurance for specified provisions. Excludes reimbursements for services rendered as described in §200.502(h) and (i). See section-specific inclusions and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal interest
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §200.330 or when used with acquisition/improvement of real property, equipment, or supplies under a Federal award, the dollar amount equal to (percentage of Federal participation in total cost) × (current fair market value of the property/improvements to extent costs were included as project costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal program
rubrics_metrics.description: All Federal awards assigned a single Assistance Listing Number, or when none assigned, all Federal awards from the same agency made for the same purpose; clusters of programs are treated per definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clusters (R&D, SFA, other) are exceptions; see definition of cluster of programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal share
rubrics_metrics.description: The portion of the Federal award costs paid using Federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final cost objective
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost objective that has allocated to it both direct and indirect costs and serves as one of the final accumulation points in the recipient's/subrecipient's accumulation system (e.g., a particular award or internal project).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See definitions of cost objective and intermediate cost objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders placed for property and services, contracts and subawards made, and similar transactions requiring payment by a recipient or subrecipient under a Federal award that will result in expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed amount award
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of grant or cooperative agreement where the agency provides a specific amount without regard to actual costs incurred; reduces administrative burden and record-keeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountability is based on performance and results. See §§200.102(c), 200.101(b), 200.201(b), and 200.333.

rubrics_metrics.name: For-profit organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally an organization organized for the purpose of earning a profit; includes S corporations, corporations, partnerships, LLCs/LLPs, and sole proprietorships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity located in a country other than the United States subject to that country's laws; includes private NGOs soliciting cash from the public, certain charitable organizations not universities/hospitals/research-only entities, and entities in countries not recognized as foreign public entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition is irrespective of citizenship of staff or place of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign public entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes a foreign government or governmental entity; public international organizations; entities owned/controlled by a foreign government; or any entity wholly/partially consisting of foreign governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public international organizations are those entitled to privileges/exemptions under the International Organizations Immunities Act (22 U.S.C. 288-288f).

rubrics_metrics.name: General purpose equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment not limited to research/medical/scientific/technical activities; examples include office equipment, modular offices, telephone networks, IT equipment/systems, air conditioning, reproduction/printing equipment, and motor vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See equipment and special purpose equipment definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the meaning specified in accounting standards issued by GASB and FASB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generally accepted government auditing standards (GAGAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Also known as the Yellow Book; means GAGAS issued by the Comptroller General of the United States, which apply to financial audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant agreement or grant
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal instrument of financial assistance used to transfer anything of value to carry out a public purpose and distinguished from a cooperative agreement by lack of substantial Federal involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include agreements providing only direct cash assistance to individuals, subsidies, loans, loan guarantees, or insurance. Consistent with 31 U.S.C. 6302, 6304, and 31 U.S.C. 6101(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest-level owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The entity that owns or controls an immediate owner of an applicant or owns/controls entities that control an immediate owner; no entity owns or exercises control of the highest-level owner as defined in FAR (48 CFR 52.204-17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility licensed as a hospital under State law or operated as a hospital by the United States, a State, or a subdivision of a State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper payment
rubrics_metrics.description: A payment that should not have been made or was made in an incorrect amount under statutory, contractual, administrative, or other legally applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes payments to ineligible recipients, for ineligible goods/services, duplicate payments, payments for goods/services not received (except where authorized by law), unauthorized payments, and payments not accounting for applicable discounts. See OMB Circular A-123 Appendix C for additional payment integrity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Tribe
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Indian Tribe, band, nation, or other organized group or community (including Alaska Native villages and regional/village corporations) recognized as eligible for special programs/services provided by the U.S. to Indians because of their status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Tribes identified in the Bureau of Indian Affairs list and entities qualifying under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act; see 25 U.S.C. 5304(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs incurred for a common or joint purpose benefitting more than one cost objective and not readily assignable to specific cost objectives without effort disproportionate to results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May require multiple indirect cost pools; pools must be distributed on a basis producing an equitable result considering relative benefits. For IHEs, often referred to as facilities & administrative (F&A) costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost rate proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation prepared by a recipient to substantiate its request to establish an indirect cost rate as described in appendices III–VII and appendix IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information technology systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Means computing devices, ancillary equipment, software, firmware, related procedures, services (including support services), and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also definitions of computing devices and equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution of Higher Education (IHE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined at 20 U.S.C. 1001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intangible property
rubrics_metrics.description: Property having no physical existence, such as trademarks, copyrights, data (including data licenses), websites, IP licenses, trade secrets, patents, patent applications, loans, notes, lease agreements, stocks, or other instruments of property ownership including software or software subscriptions/licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate cost objective
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost objective used to accumulate indirect or service center costs that are subsequently allocated to one or more indirect cost pools or final cost objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cost objective and final cost objective definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes designed and implemented by recipients and subrecipients to provide reasonable assurance regarding achievement of objectives in: (1) effectiveness and efficiency of operations; (2) reliability of reporting; and (3) compliance with laws and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal loan or loan guarantee received or administered by a recipient or subrecipient, except as used in definition of program income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes direct loans, direct loan obligations, loan guarantees, and loan guarantee commitments, with specific definitions for each; excludes acquisition of a federally guaranteed loan in satisfaction of default claims or Commodity Credit Corporation price support loans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local government
rubrics_metrics.description: Any unit of government within a State such as county, borough, municipality, city, town, township, parish, local public authority (including public housing agencies), special district, school district, intrastate district, council of governments, or other agency/instrumentality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major program
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal program determined by the auditor to be a major program under §200.518 or identified as a major program by a Federal agency/pass-through entity under §200.503(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency's or pass-through entity's written determination, provided to the auditee, of the adequacy of the auditee's proposed corrective actions addressing audit findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on evaluation of audit findings and proposed corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual procurement transaction for supplies or services where the aggregate amount does not exceed the micro-purchase threshold; part of small purchases using informal procurement methods under §200.320.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-purchase threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The dollar amount at or below which micro-purchase procedures may be used; generally not to exceed the FAR amount unless higher amount is requested and approved by the cognizant agency for indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients/subrecipients responsible for determining appropriate threshold (≤ FAR amount) based on internal controls, risk evaluation, and documented procurement procedures; consider local government purchasing laws. Threshold must never exceed FAR value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified Total Direct Cost (MTDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means all direct salaries and wages, applicable fringe benefits, materials and supplies, services, travel, and up to the first $50,000 of each subaward (regardless of period of performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes equipment, capital expenditures, patient care charges, rental costs, tuition remission, scholarships/fellowships, participant support costs, and the portion of each subaward in excess of $50,000. Other exclusions allowed only to avoid serious inequity with approval of cognizant agency for indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discretionary award
rubrics_metrics.description: An award made by the Federal agency to specific recipients in accordance with statutory, eligibility, and compliance requirements where the agency cannot exercise judgment in awarding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award amount may be specifically determined or by formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Federal entity (NFE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a State, local government, Indian Tribe, IHE, or nonprofit organization carrying out a Federal award as a recipient or subrecipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit organization
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization operated primarily for scientific, educational, service, charitable, or similar public interest purposes, not organized primarily for profit, using net proceeds to maintain/expand operations, and not an IHE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of funding opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal announcement of the availability of Federal funding describing who is eligible, evaluation criteria, required application components, and how to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be called program announcement, notice of funding availability, broad agency announcement, research announcement, solicitation, or other terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the Executive Office of the President, Office of Management and Budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversight agency for audit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency providing the predominant amount of direct funding (as listed on the schedule of expenditures of Federal awards) to a recipient/subrecipient unless OMB designates a cognizant agency for audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If direct funding <25% of total Federal expenditures, the agency with predominant total funding is the oversight agency. If no direct funding, the predominant pass-through funding agency assumes oversight. Duties and reassignment process in §200.513(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally an individual participating in or attending program activities under a Federal award (e.g., trainings or conferences) who is not responsible for implementation of the Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include individuals committing effort to development/delivery of program activities (consultants, project personnel, staff). Examples: community members, public whose input is sought, students, conference attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs that support participants and their involvement in a Federal award, such as stipends, subsistence allowances, travel allowances, registration fees, temporary dependent care, and per diem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid directly to or on behalf of participants; see Participant definition in §200.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-through entity
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient or subrecipient that provides a subaward to a subrecipient (including lower tier) to carry out part of a Federal program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority flows through the subaward agreement; see §200.331 for criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance goal
rubrics_metrics.description: A measurable target level of performance expressed as a tangible, measurable objective against which actual achievement can be compared, including quantitative standards, values, or rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some instances (e.g., discretionary research awards) may be limited to requirement to submit technical performance reports to be evaluated per agency policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The time interval between the start and end date of a Federal award, which may include one or more budget periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of the period of performance in the Federal award (consistent with §200.211(b)(5)) does not commit the agency to fund beyond the currently approved budget period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal property
rubrics_metrics.description: Property other than real property; may be tangible or intangible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See definitions of real property and personal property in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity alone or when combined with other information linked or linkable to a specific individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not attached to any single category; requires case-by-case assessment of identification risk. Non-PII can become PII when combined with additional public information in any medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The written approval obtained in advance by an authorized official of a Federal agency or pass-through entity of certain costs or programmatic decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific prior approval requirements are detailed elsewhere in the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross income earned by the recipient or subrecipient directly generated by a supported activity or earned as a result of the Federal award during the period of performance, except as provided in §200.307(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes fees for services, use/rental of property acquired under awards, sale of commodities fabricated under award, license fees, royalties, and principal/interest on loans made with award funds. Interest on advances of Federal funds is not program income. Generally does not include rebates, credits, discounts, and related interest; see §200.407 and 35 U.S.C. 200-212 for disposition of rights in educational awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Total allowable costs incurred under a Federal award and all cost sharing, including third-party contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property
rubrics_metrics.description: Means real property or personal property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See this section's definitions of real property and personal property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected Personally Identifiable Information (Protected PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: PII except for PII that must be disclosed by law; includes sensitive identifiers and records such as SSN, passport number, credit card numbers, biometrics, dates/places of birth, mother's maiden name, criminal/medical/financial records, and educational transcripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioned cost
rubrics_metrics.description: An amount expended or received from a Federal award that in the auditor's judgment is (i) noncompliant or suspected noncompliant with statutes/regulations/award terms; (ii) at audit time lacked adequate documentation to support compliance; or (iii) appeared unreasonable and not reflecting actions a prudent person would take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph clarifies calculation of questioned costs for documentation deficiencies, notes exceptions where there is no questioned cost solely for internal control deficiencies or certain reporting-type noncompliance, distinguishes known and likely questioned costs, and states questioned costs are not improper payments until reviewed/confirmed per OMB A-123 Appendix C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real property
rubrics_metrics.description: Land, including land improvements, structures, appurtenances, and legal interests in land (fee interest, licenses, rights of way, easements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes moveable machinery and equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity that receives a Federal award directly from a Federal agency to carry out an activity under a Federal program; does not include subrecipients or individuals that are participants or beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal award
rubrics_metrics.description: A Federal award for which the start date is contiguous with, or closely follows, the end of the expiring Federal award, beginning a new and distinct period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Development (R&D)
rubrics_metrics.description: All basic and applied research activities and all development activities performed by a recipient or subrecipient; includes training in research techniques using the same facilities and not part of instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research is systematic study toward fuller scientific knowledge; development uses knowledge from research to produce useful materials, devices, systems, or methods (including prototypes/processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified acquisition threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The dollar amount below which small purchase methods may be used to expedite purchases; recipients/subrecipients adopt small purchase procedures for items at or below this threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses FAR amount at 48 CFR part 2, subpart 2.1 as baseline; recipient/subrecipient responsible for determining appropriate threshold ≤ FAR amount based on internal controls, risk, and procurement procedures and must ensure local purchasing laws compliance. Threshold must never exceed FAR amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special purpose equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment used only for research, medical, scientific, or similar technical activities; examples include microscopes, x-ray machines, surgical instruments, spectrometers, and associated software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See equipment and general purpose equipment definitions for distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State of the United States, the District of Columbia, Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, and any agency or instrumentality thereof exclusive of local governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Financial Aid (SFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal awards under programs of general student assistance (e.g., Title IV HEA) administered by the Department of Education and similar programs by other agencies; excludes fellowships or similar awards on a competitive basis or for specified studies/research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward
rubrics_metrics.description: An award provided by a pass-through entity to a subrecipient for the subrecipient to contribute to goals/objectives of the project by carrying out part of a Federal award received by the pass-through entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include payments to a contractor, beneficiary, or participant. May be in any form of legal agreement consistent with §200.331, including agreements a pass-through entity considers a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity that receives a subaward from a pass-through entity to carry out part of a Federal award; does not include a beneficiary or participant. A subrecipient may also be a direct recipient of other Federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary
rubrics_metrics.description: An entity in which more than 50 percent is owned or controlled directly by a parent corporation or through another subsidiary of a parent corporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply
rubrics_metrics.description: All tangible personal property other than equipment; a computing device is a supply if acquisition cost is below the lesser of recipient's capitalization level or $10,000 regardless of useful life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See definitions of computing devices and equipment for distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecommunications cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of using communication technologies such as mobile phones, landlines, and the internet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The action a Federal agency or pass-through entity takes to discontinue a Federal award, in whole or in part, before the planned end date of the period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination does not include discontinuing an award due to lack of available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party in-kind contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of non-cash contributions (property or services) that benefit a project or program and are contributed by non-Federal third parties without charge to a recipient or subrecipient under a Federal award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unliquidated financial obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial obligations incurred by the recipient or subrecipient but not paid (liquidated) for financial reports prepared on a cash basis; for accrual reports, obligations incurred but expenditures not recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unobligated balance
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of funds under a Federal award that the recipient or subrecipient has not obligated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed by subtracting cumulative unliquidated obligations and expenditures from the cumulative amount the agency or pass-through entity authorized the recipient/subrecipient to obligate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary committed cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing specifically pledged voluntarily in the proposal's budget by the recipient or subrecipient which becomes a binding requirement of the Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §200.306 for cost sharing/matching policies.
